children.title: Blossom Expansion
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-graph matching structure from a contracted blossom.

knowledge_statements.title: Blossom Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifting a contracted augmenting path through an odd alternating blossom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an augmenting path \(P'\) for \(M/B\) in \(G/B\), together with the stored boundary endpoints of blossom \(B\). If \(P'\) avoids the pseudovertex \(\beta\), return the same path in \(G\). Otherwise replace the segment through \(\beta\) by the parity-compatible alternating arc of \(B\) joining the recorded boundary endpoint to the base or to the other recorded boundary endpoint. Choose the one of the two cycle arcs that preserves alternation with the entering and leaving edges. The resulting path \(P\) is augmenting for \(M\); output \(M\triangle E(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a contracted pseudovertex on an augmenting path by the blossom arc whose parity preserves alternation, then augment.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a contracted odd alternating blossom for \(M\).
\(P'\) is an augmenting path for \(M/B\), with original boundary endpoints retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Expansion yields an \(M\)-augmenting path \(P\) in \(G\), and \(M\triangle E(P)\) has cardinality \(|M|+1\).

notation.meaning: augmenting path in the contracted graph

children.title: Contraction Invariants
children.top_down_role: Matching-relevant structure preserved by blossom contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Contraction Invariants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Augmenting-path invariance under valid Edmonds blossom shrinking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a blossom detected in an alternating search for matching \(M\), and let \(G/B\) and \(M/B\) be obtained by valid blossom contraction. Then \(G\) contains an \(M\)-augmenting path if and only if \(G/B\) contains an \(M/B\)-augmenting path. Any contracted augmenting path can be expanded through \(B\) to an augmenting path in \(G\), while contraction maps an augmenting path in \(G\), after the standard simplification of repeated blossom crossings, to one in \(G/B\). Therefore contraction preserves the test that \(M\) is maximum and preserves the possibility of increasing its cardinality by one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid blossom contraction preserves the existence of an augmenting path and hence preserves whether the current matching is maximum.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite undirected graph and \(M\) is a matching.
\(B\) is a valid alternating blossom produced by an Edmonds search.
\(G/B\) and \(M/B\) use the standard base-preserving contraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) has an \(M\)-augmenting path if and only if \(G/B\) has an \(M/B\)-augmenting path.

notation.meaning: graph obtained by contracting blossom B

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Augmenting-Path Preservation under Blossom Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the bidirectional augmenting-path existence invariant validating blossom contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a matching in a graph \(G\), and suppose that an augmenting-path search from a vertex \(u\) discovers a blossom \(b\). Then an augmenting path from \(u\) exists in \(G\) with respect to \(M\) if and only if an augmenting path exists in \(G/b\) with respect to \(M/b\), starting from \(u\), except that the starting vertex is \(v_b\) when \(u\) is the basis of \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contracting a discovered blossom preserves the existence of an augmenting path from the search vertex; when that vertex is the blossom basis, the contracted vertex is used instead.
assumptions_latex: b\text{ is a blossom discovered during an augmenting-path search from }u
G/b\text{ and }M/b\text{ are the corresponding contractions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ an }M\text{-augmenting path from }u\text{ in }G\iff\exists\text{ an }(M/b)\text{-augmenting path from }u'\text{ in }G/b,\quad u'=\begin{cases}v_b,&u\text{ is the basis of }b,\\u,&\text{otherwise}\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a contracted alternating walk use \(\beta\). Expanding \(\beta\) requires an alternating path inside \(B\) joining the prescribed external incidence or incidences to the blossom base with parity compatible with \(M\). If the contraction record omits the base, cyclic child order, or the attachment vertices of contracted edges, two distinct internal alternating lifts may agree after contraction, and an arbitrary lift may repeat a vertex or place two consecutive matched or unmatched edges. Thus contraction alone does not define expansion; expansion is valid only relative to retained blossom state sufficient to select a simple alternating lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contracted blossom cannot always be expanded from the pseudovertex alone. Its base, internal order, and external attachment vertices must be retained to select a valid alternating lift.

source_refs.locator: Section 5. Cardinality Matching Algorithm p. 193

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nested-blossom representation consists of a laminar family \(\mathcal B\) of odd vertex sets. Each nontrivial \(B\in\mathcal B\) stores a base \(b(B)\), an odd cyclic sequence of maximal proper child blossoms and singleton vertices, and the cycle edges joining consecutive children. Laminarity means that for \(B,C\in\mathcal B\), either \(B\cap C=\varnothing\), \(B\subseteq C\), or \(C\subseteq B\). Inclusion therefore forms a rooted forest. Recursively replacing every child by its stored cycle reconstructs \(B\), while the stored base and matching parity determine the alternating route used when an augmenting path is expanded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested blossoms form a laminar inclusion forest. Each blossom stores a base and an odd cycle of children, enabling recursive reconstruction and parity-correct expansion.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Blossom Representations

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph with \(n=|V|\), \(m=|E|\), and current matching \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method computes a maximum-cardinality matching in \(O(m\sqrt n)\) time in the unit-cost RAM model.

notation.meaning: length of a shortest augmenting path

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical unweighted general-graph Micali–Vazirani bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A phase begins by determining \(\ell(M)\), the minimum number of edges in an \(M\)-augmenting path, using alternating levels together with blossom formation. It then finds and augments along a maximal collection of vertex-disjoint augmenting paths of length \(\ell(M)\), represented and expanded through the phase's blossom structure. The phase ends when no augmenting path at that level remains. After augmentation, the next existing shortest augmenting path is longer. With linear-time search work \(O(m)\) per phase and \(O(\sqrt n)\) phases, the total running time is \(O(m\sqrt n)\), and termination with no augmenting path certifies maximum cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Micali–Vazirani organizes general-graph matching into shortest-augmenting-path phases. Linear work per phase over at most square-root-many phases yields the classical O(m sqrt n) bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Micali–Vazirani Phase-Based Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The classical bound is plausible and the complexity-bound role fits, but no citation supports the precise phase invariant, linear work per phase, or number of phases.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(M=\varnothing\). For each augmentation search, grow an alternating forest \(F\) from all \(M\)-exposed vertices. When an eligible edge reaches a new vertex, add the corresponding unmatched and matched forest edges. When it joins two appropriate outer vertices in one tree, contract the resulting odd alternating cycle and record it in \(\mathcal B\). When it joins outer vertices rooted at distinct exposed vertices, trace the forest paths and blossom records to obtain an augmenting path \(P\), replace \(M\) by \(M\triangle E(P)\), expand affected blossoms, and restart. If a complete search finds no augmenting path, output \(M\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-adjustment iteration of Edmonds' weighted perfect-matching algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes one primal–dual iteration on the contracted tight-edge graph, including optimality, infeasibility, and bounded-update outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $z$ be a feasible dual solution and let $G_z$ be the current contracted tight-edge graph. Compute a maximum-cardinality matching $M$ in $G_z$. If $M$ is perfect, expand it to a perfect matching of $G$ using only tight edges; under the maintained optimality conditions, this matching is optimal. Otherwise, form the Gallai--Edmonds decomposition $W,X,Y$ of $G_z$. If $B(v)\in\mathcal B$ is the vertex set contracted to $v$, decrease $z_{B(v)}$ by $\varepsilon$ for every $v\in X$, and for every connected component $C$ of $G_z[Y]$ increase $z_A$ by $\varepsilon$, where $A=\bigcup_{v\in C}B(v)$. Choose the largest $\varepsilon>0$ preserving dual feasibility. Tight matching edges remain tight, and
\[
\#\operatorname{cc}(G_z[Y])>|X|,
\]
so the dual objective increases by
\[
\varepsilon\bigl(\#\operatorname{cc}(G_z[Y])-|X|\bigr)\geq\varepsilon.
\]
If arbitrarily large $\varepsilon$ remains feasible, the dual LP is unbounded, the primal perfect-matching LP is infeasible, and $G$ has no perfect matching. Otherwise, update $G_z$ to reflect newly tight edges, contractions, and unpackings, and continue. The stated finiteness argument uses the fact that between augmentations every grow, shrink, or unpack step increases the number of outer vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a maximum matching in the current contracted tight-edge graph. If it is perfect, expand it through tight edges to obtain an optimal perfect matching. Otherwise, use the Gallai–Edmonds decomposition to decrease dual variables associated with X and increase variables associated with components of Y, taking the largest positive step that preserves dual feasibility. This preserves tight matching edges and raises the dual objective. If the step is unbounded, no perfect matching exists; otherwise new tight edges, contractions, or unpackings produce the next iteration. Finiteness is tied to growth in the number of outer vertices between augmentations.
assumptions_latex: z\text{ is feasible for the weighted perfect-matching dual}
G_z\text{ is the current contracted graph formed from tight edges}
B(v)\in\mathcal B\text{ denotes the vertex set contracted to }v
\text{The algorithm maintains the cited primal--dual optimality conditions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The iteration returns an optimal perfect matching, certifies that no perfect matching exists when the dual step is unbounded, or performs a maximal dual-feasible update with strictly increased dual objective.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Laminar primal–dual blossom procedure for minimum-weight perfect matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted perfect matching in a simple general graph known to admit a perfect matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be simple and admit a perfect matching. Maintain a laminar collection \(\Omega\) of odd subsets of \(V\), dual values \(\pi:\Omega\to\mathbb Q\) satisfying the stated dual-feasibility invariant, a matching \(M\) in the contracted tight-edge graph \(G'=G_\pi/\Omega\), and a stored circuit \(C_U\) for every nonsingleton \(U\in\Omega\). Iteratively augment along an alternating augmenting path, shrink the circuit of an alternating flower, or make a maximal feasible dual adjustment and deshrink a nonsingleton set whose dual value reaches zero. If \(M\) becomes perfect in \(G'\), it expands to a perfect matching \(N\) of \(G\) satisfying \(w_\pi(N)=0\) and \(|N\cap\delta(U)|=1\) for every \(U\in\Omega\); hence \(N\) is minimum-weight. If \(V\ne\varnothing\), laminarity also gives \(|\Omega|\le 2|V|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted primal–dual blossom procedure maintains feasible dual values, a laminar family of odd sets, and a matching in a contracted tight-edge graph. Its steps augment the matching, shrink a blossom, adjust the dual values, or expand a zero-valued blossom. A perfect contracted matching expands to a minimum-weight perfect matching, and the maintained laminar family has at most twice as many sets as vertices when the graph is nonempty.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) has at least one perfect matching.
\(\Omega\) is a laminar collection of odd-cardinality subsets of \(V\).
\(\pi:\Omega\to\mathbb Q\) satisfies the stated dual-feasibility invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\text{ perfect in }G'\Rightarrow N\text{ is a minimum-weight perfect matching of }G,\ w_\pi(N)=0,\ |N\cap\delta(U)|=1\ \forall U\in\Omega;\quad V\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow |\Omega|\le2|V|.\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amortized implementation of weighted primal–dual perfect matching in general graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain the laminar blossom family \(\Omega\), dual values \(\pi\), matching \(M\), stored blossom circuits, and an \(M\)-alternating forest \(F\) in the contracted tight-edge graph. Represent the contracted graph implicitly by minimum reduced-weight edges \(e_{YZ}\), forest-facing minima \(e_Y\), and potentials \(p(v)=\sum_{U\in\Omega:\,v\in U}\pi(U)\). Each dual update triggers forest growth, matching augmentation, blossom contraction, or blossom expansion. There are at most n iterations and O(n squared) work between matching augmentations, giving O(n cubed) total time.

The graph admits a perfect matching.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an even integer \(n\) and a symmetric matrix \([c_{ij}]\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{n\times n}\), initialize the vertex labels \(\alpha_i=\tfrac12\min_j c_{ij}\), all blossom labels \(\gamma_k=0\), and \(M=\varnothing\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each vertex \(v\in V\), the equality constraint \(x(\delta(v))=1\) has a free dual variable \(y_v\in\mathbb R\). Together with odd-set variables, dual feasibility requires, for every edge \(uv\in E\), \[y_u+y_v+\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq V:\ |S|\text{ odd},\ uv\in E(S)}}z_S\ge w_{uv}.\] The vertex contribution to the reduced slack of \(uv\) is therefore \(y_u+y_v\). Translating one vertex coordinate changes all incident edge slacks uniformly, while feasibility is preserved exactly when every affected edge inequality remains nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each degree equality produces a free vertex dual variable. An edge receives the sum of its endpoint variables, so changing one coordinate uniformly changes all incident edge slacks.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal odd-set inequality is \[x(E(S))\le \frac{|S|-1}{2}.\] Its dual coordinate satisfies \(z_S\ge0\), contributes \(z_S\) to the covering inequality of every edge in \(E(S)\), contributes nothing to edges crossing \(\delta(S)\), and has objective coefficient \((|S|-1)/2\). Hence increasing \(z_S\) translates the dual load of all internal edges together. Complementary slackness implies that \(z_S>0\) can occur in an optimal complementary pair only when the matching uses exactly \((|S|-1)/2\) edges of \(E(S)\), equivalently exactly one matching edge crosses \(\delta(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An odd-set dual variable is nonnegative, prices every edge internal to that odd set, and can be positive complementarily only when the matching leaves exactly one vertex matched outward.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(L_{uv}=y_u+y_v+\sum_{S:uv\in E(S)}z_S\). Dual feasibility gives \(L_e\ge w_e\) for every \(e\in E\). If \(L_e=w_e\) for every \(e\in M\), and \(z_S>0\) implies \(x(E(S))=(|S|-1)/2\), then all complementary-slackness products vanish. Consequently the primal weight \(\sum_{e\in M}w_e\) equals the dual objective \(\sum_{v\in V}y_v+\sum_S((|S|-1)/2)z_S\). Weak duality then certifies that \(M\) is a maximum-weight perfect matching and \((y,z)\) is dual-optimal.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \(s_e=L_e-w_e\) and form \(E_0=\{e\in E:s_e=0\}\). Initialize an alternating forest at exposed vertices of the contracted graph. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an alternating forest in \(G/\mathcal B\), treating each maximal blossom as one pseudovertex with the parity of its base. When a scanned tight edge joins two outer vertices in one search tree, trace their paths to the least common ancestor, contract the resulting odd alternating cycle, record its base and children, and continue on the new quotient. When a tight edge joins distinct exposed-root trees, concatenate their forest paths and that edge, then recursively expand every encountered blossom according to its stored entry, exit, and base. The resulting simple alternating path is used to augment \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search treats maximal blossoms as pseudovertex units. New odd cycles are contracted, while stored bases and child structure allow any discovered augmenting path to be expanded correctly.

knowledge_statements.title: Tight-Blossom Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural invariant of active blossoms in weighted equality-subgraph search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every edge \(e\) on the defining alternating cycle of \(B\), tightness means \(L_e=w_e\). The cycle is odd and has a distinguished base; its edges alternate between \(M\) and \(E\setminus M\) except at the base. With the base, child order, and attachment vertices retained, contraction preserves the alternating-search structure and the stored decomposition supplies parity-compatible lifts. Moreover, if a feasible perfect matching \(M^\star\) and the dual solution are complementary and \(z_B>0\), then \(|M^\star\cap E(B)|=(|B|-1)/2\), equivalently exactly one edge of \(M^\star\) crosses \(\delta(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight blossom is an odd alternating cycle of zero-slack edges with a stored base and decomposition, permitting contraction and later parity-correct lifting. In a complementary perfect matching, a positive blossom dual value forces exactly one matching edge to leave the blossom.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite, \(M\subseteq E\) is a matching, and \((y,z)\) is dual-feasible for the maximum-weight perfect-matching formulation.
\(B\subseteq V\) is an active odd blossom whose defining alternating cycle consists of tight edges and whose base, child order, and edge attachments are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The blossom is an admissible contracted search unit; if a feasible perfect matching \(M^\star\) is complementary to the dual and \(z_B>0\), exactly one edge of \(M^\star\) crosses \(\delta(B)\).

children.title: Search-Stall Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Stall Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-stall condition stated independently of the sign convention used by a particular weighted-matching dual update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tight-edge search stalls when every tight edge incident with the outer set \(O\) has been scanned and none permits forest growth, blossom contraction, or augmentation. The stall condition alone is not an optimality certificate. To resume the search, the particular primal–dual algorithm must choose a nonzero update that preserves dual feasibility, nonnegativity of all constrained odd-set variables, and the tight equalities required by the current forest and matching. A maximal finite update ends when a previously slack search-relevant edge becomes tight or an active blossom variable reaches zero. The first event enlarges the equality-subgraph search, while the second permits the algorithm to dissolve or expand the affected blossom. If no such positive update is available, termination requires a separate optimality or infeasibility argument supplied by the selected algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search stalls when all reachable tight edges have been exhausted without growth, contraction, or augmentation. A variant-specific feasible dual update must then create a relevant tight edge or reduce an active blossom price to zero; the absence of such an update is not by itself an optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: \((y,z)\) is dual-feasible and an alternating tight-edge search has reached outer set \(O\) and inner set \(I\).
No currently tight edge permits forest growth, blossom contraction, or augmentation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Further search progress requires a feasible nonzero dual update that creates a new search-relevant tight edge or makes an active blossom variable zero; otherwise a separate terminality certificate is required.

children.title: Gabow Weighted-Matching Methods
children.top_down_role: Gabow-style combinatorial methods for weighted general-graph matching.

assumptions_latex: \(w:E\to\mathbb Z\) is an integral edge-weight function.
The objective is to find a matching maximizing \(w(M)=\sum_{e\in M}w(e)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final matching maximizes \(w(M)\) over all matchings of \(G\).

notation.meaning: Dual variables associated with vertices and contracted odd sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact integral-weight scaling template; the precise Gabow variant and its complexity remain source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(G=(V,E)\) and integral weights \(w\), initialize \(M=\varnothing\), feasible vertex and blossom dual variables \((y,z)\), and a scaling unit \(\delta\) determined by the leading weight bits. At each scale, form truncated weights \(w_\delta\), restore the prescribed approximate domination and tightness conditions for reduced costs, and repeatedly perform searches in the eligible-edge graph. Each search either augments \(M\), contracts an odd alternating blossom, expands a blossom whose dual reaches its boundary, or changes \((y,z)\) by the largest admissible dual adjustment. After no further augmentation is possible at that scale, refine \(w_\delta\), reduce \(\delta\), and continue. When the exact scale is reached, output \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process integral weights from coarse to fine while maintaining matching and blossom dual invariants; eligible-edge searches and dual adjustments yield an exact maximum-weight matching at the final scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Gabow Weighted-Matching Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No evidence is cited, and the approximate domination, tightness, eligibility, and termination conditions depend on the particular Gabow scaling variant. The exact-optimality conclusion cannot be checked until a variant and supporting source are specified.

assumptions_latex: \(w:E\to\mathbb Z\) and \(|w(e)|\le W\) for every \(e\in E\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=1+\lceil\log_2 W\rceil\). A binary weight-scaling regime chooses an initial power-of-two unit \(\delta_0\ge W\) and sets \(\delta_{k+1}=\delta_k/2\). At phase \(k\), the algorithm uses a truncated or rounded weight function \(w_k\) exposing the weight information resolved at unit \(\delta_k\), while preserving an approximate primal-dual optimality invariant whose error is proportional to \(\delta_k\). Once \(\delta_k\) reaches the unit scale, integrality converts the final approximate invariant into exact optimality. Consequently, only \(L\) binary refinement phases are required; multiplying all weights by a positive common integer changes numerical magnitudes but not the optimizing matchings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary scaling reveals integral weights one bit at a time. Weights bounded by W require at most one plus the ceiling of log base two of W phases.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scaling phase at unit \(\delta\) consists of four logical operations. First, incorporate the next weight information and modify dual variables so approximate domination is restored. Second, construct the eligible graph \(H_\delta\) from edges meeting the phase's reduced-cost threshold. Third, run alternating-forest searches in \(H_\delta\), augmenting \(M\) when an augmenting path is found and maintaining odd blossoms by contraction and expansion. Fourth, when a search stalls, perform a maximal admissible dual adjustment; repeat until the phase termination condition holds. The resulting matching, blossom family, and dual variables satisfy the initialization invariant for scale \(\delta/2\). At the terminal integral scale, complementary slackness yields exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each scale imports finer weight information, restores dual feasibility, searches eligible edges with blossom operations, and performs dual adjustments until the next scale can begin.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Phase Structure

children.title: Numerical Weight Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Dependence on weight magnitude, integrality, or encoding.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Weight Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-length and overflow boundary for exact integral-weight implementations under an explicit sign-magnitude convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a signed integer is stored in sign-magnitude form using one sign bit and \(b-1\) magnitude bits. Such a word represents every integer of magnitude at most \(2^{b-1}-1\). Hence all input weights satisfying \(|w(e)|\le W\) are representable exactly if and only if \(W\le 2^{b-1}-1\), equivalently \(b\ge 1+\lceil\log_2(W+1)\rceil\). Because a matching contains at most \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) edges, its objective value has magnitude at most \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor W\); an objective accumulator therefore requires at least \(1+\lceil\log_2(\lfloor n/2\rfloor W+1)\rceil\) bits under the same convention. Scaled weights, reduced costs, and dual expressions require separate bounds. Overflow or inexact arithmetic can change eligibility tests and invalidate an optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With one sign bit and b minus one magnitude bits, exact input storage requires b at least one plus the ceiling of log base two of W plus one. Matching-value accumulators and other derived quantities may require additional bits, and overflow can invalidate eligibility and optimality tests.
assumptions_latex: \(w:E\to\mathbb Z\) and \(|w(e)|\le W\) for every \(e\in E\), where \(W\ge 0\).
Signed integers use a sign-magnitude representation with one sign bit and \(b-1\) magnitude bits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact input storage requires \(b\ge 1+\lceil\log_2(W+1)\rceil\), while an objective accumulator requires at least \(1+\lceil\log_2(\lfloor n/2\rfloor W+1)\rceil\) bits under the stated convention.

notation.meaning: Total number of bits in a sign-magnitude signed-integer word.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store a weighted graph in a symmetric matrix \(A\), where \(A_{uv}=w(uv)\) when \(uv\in E\) and a distinguished sentinel denotes \(uv\notin E\). Edge existence and weight lookup then take \(O(1)\) time, the matrix occupies \(\Theta(n^2)\) words, and scanning every possible edge takes \(O(n^2)\) time. Consequently, when \(m=\Theta(n^2)\), matrix storage is asymptotically commensurate with the input size and supports simple implementations of reduced-cost scans, alternating-forest growth, and blossom adjacency tests. This representation statement does not by itself determine the total running time, which also depends on the number of searches and dual-adjustment events.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each undirected edge \(uv\in E\) by linked or indexed records appearing in \(L(u)\) and \(L(v)\), with a shared identifier for its weight and matching status. The representation occupies \(O(n+m)\) words, enumerates the edges incident with \(v\) in \(O(|L(v)|)\) time, and scans all stored edges in \(O(m)\) time. Sparse storage avoids inspecting nonedges, although priority queues or additional indices may be required to locate the next minimum-slack edge efficiently during primal-dual adjustments.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An integer-weight implementation is exact when every stored weight, scaled weight, reduced cost, dual variable, and objective accumulator is represented without overflow and every comparison is exact. In a word-RAM analysis, arithmetic may be counted as \(O(1)\) only if the implementation establishes that all derived integers fit within \(B\)-bit words. Rational weights may be converted to integers by a common positive denominator, but the resulting encoding length, rather than numerical value alone, governs arithmetic cost.

children.title: Density–Encoding Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Performance interactions between graph density plus weight representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Density–Encoding Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint density and binary-encoding contribution to scan-based running time; the bound excludes non-scan work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=1+\lceil\log_2 W\rceil\). If a binary scaling implementation performs \(s_k\) complete edge scans during phase \(k\), then its total scan time is \(O\!\left(m\sum_{k=1}^{L}s_k\right)\) with adjacency lists and \(O\!\left(n^2\sum_{k=1}^{L}s_k\right)\) with a matrix. Thus sparse storage improves the scan component when \(m=o(n^2)\) and searches avoid nonedges, whereas matrix storage has asymptotically commensurate size when \(m=\Theta(n^2)\). The number \(L\) records the binary weight-encoding contribution and is distinct from graph density. These bounds exclude blossom maintenance, priority operations, arithmetic bit cost, and other search or dual-update work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Density determines the cost of each complete edge scan, while binary weight encoding determines the number of scaling phases. If phase k performs s sub k scans, the scan costs sum over those multiplicities; other algorithmic work must be charged separately.
assumptions_latex: \(w:E\to\mathbb Z\) satisfies \(|w(e)|\le W\) for every \(e\in E\), where \(W\ge1\).
The implementation uses \(L=1+\lceil\log_2 W\rceil\) binary scaling phases and performs \(s_k\ge0\) complete edge scans in phase \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scan time is \(O\!\left(m\sum_{k=1}^{L}s_k\right)\) with adjacency lists and \(O\!\left(n^2\sum_{k=1}^{L}s_k\right)\) with a matrix; these expressions do not bound the algorithm's non-scan work.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 11. Weighted Matching p. 277

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(F:\mathbb R^E\to\mathbb R\), defined by \(F(w)=\max_{M\in\mathcal M}\langle w,\chi^M\rangle\), is convex, continuous, and piecewise linear because it is the maximum of finitely many linear functions. If \(M^*\) is optimal at \(w\), then for every perturbation \(d\in\mathbb R^E\), \[F(w+d)\ge F(w)+\langle d,\chi^{M^*}\rangle.\] Thus \(\chi^{M^*}\in\partial F(w)\). More generally, \(\partial F(w)\) is the convex hull of incidence vectors of all matchings optimal at \(w\). A unique optimum remains optimal under every sufficiently small perturbation that stays inside its normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal matching value is convex and piecewise linear in edge weights. Optimal matching incidence vectors are exactly the extreme data governing its local sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edmonds LP Characterization of General Weighted Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded characterization using the source's previously defined constraints (11.1)–(11.2), subset family, and parameters; these definitions are not expanded in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For costs \(\{c_{ij}:1\le i<j\le n\}\), the general matching problem is equivalent to minimizing \(\sum_{i,j}c_{ij}x_{ij}\) subject to (11.1), (11.2), and, for each indexed subset \(S_k\), \(\sum_{i,j\in S_k}x_{ij}+y_k=s_k\) with \(y_k\ge 0\), for \(k=1,\ldots,N\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matching, fractional-matching, and perfect-matching polytope hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the three polytopes, their containments, the perfect-matching face, and failure of the fractional relaxation to describe the matching polytope in general graphs. The extracted span does not reproduce system (7.1.5).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a graph with \(p\) vertices. The matching polytope \(M(G)\) is the convex hull of the incidence vectors of all matchings of \(G\); the fractional matching polytope \(FM(G)\) is the solution polytope of system (7.1.5); and the perfect-matching polytope \(PM(G)\) is the convex hull of the incidence vectors of all perfect matchings of \(G\). Then \(PM(G)\subseteq M(G)\subseteq FM(G)\), and \(PM(G)\) is the face of \(M(G)\) defined by \(x(E(G))=p/2\). Equality \(M(G)=FM(G)\) need not hold for non-bipartite graphs: for a triangle, \((1/2,1/2,1/2)\) is a fractional vertex of \(FM(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matching polytope is the convex hull of all matching incidence vectors, the fractional matching polytope is the region defined by the source's system (7.1.5), and the perfect-matching polytope is the convex hull of all perfect-matching incidence vectors. The perfect-matching polytope is a face of the matching polytope, and both lie in the fractional matching polytope. The triangle shows that the latter containment can be strict outside the bipartite case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: PM(G)=\{x\in M(G):x(E(G))=p/2\}\subseteq M(G)\subseteq FM(G)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nearly Uniform-Cardinality Decomposition of a Fractional Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents any point of the general matching polytope using matchings whose cardinalities differ by at most one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected graph and $x\in P_{\mathrm{matching}}(G)$. There exist matchings $M_1,\ldots,M_r$ and coefficients $\lambda_i\ge0$ with $\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i=1$ such that $x=\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i\chi^{M_i}$ and
\[
\lfloor\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x\rfloor\le |M_i|\le\lceil\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x\rceil
\quad(i=1,\ldots,r).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point of a general matching polytope is a convex combination of matchings whose sizes are the floor or ceiling of the point's total edge weight.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edmonds's General Matching Polytope Description
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete linear description of the convex hull of all matching incidence vectors in a general graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a graph, and let \(\mathcal A\) denote the odd-cardinality subsets of \(V\). Then
\[
\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^M:M\text{ is a matching of }G\}
=\left\{x\in\mathbb R_+^E:x(\delta(v))\le1\ (v\in V),\quad x(E(G[A]))\le\frac{|A|-1}{2}\ (A\in\mathcal A)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of all matching incidence vectors is exactly the set of nonnegative edge vectors satisfying every vertex-degree inequality and every odd-set inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{\mathrm M}(G)=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^E:x(\delta(v))\le1\ (v\in V),\ x(E(G[A]))\le(|A|-1)/2\ (A\in\mathcal A)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cunningham–Marsh Integral Laminar Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral and laminar optimal dual certificates for nonnegative integer-weight matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a graph and \(w\in\mathbb Z_+^E\). In the weighted-matching dual minimum
\[
\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V}y_v+\sum_{U\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{odd}}(V)}z_U\left\lfloor\frac{|U|}{2}\right\rfloor:y,z\ge0,\ \sum_v y_v\chi^{\delta(v)}+\sum_U z_U\chi^{E[U]}\ge w\right\},
\]
there is an optimal solution with \(y\in\mathbb Z_+^V\), \(z\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal P_{\mathrm{odd}}(V)}\), and \(\{U\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{odd}}(V):z_U>0\}\) laminar.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative integer edge weights, an optimal weighted-matching dual solution can be chosen integral, with the positively weighted odd sets forming a laminar family.
assumptions_latex: y,z\text{ are feasible variables of the weighted-matching dual formula}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ an optimal }(y,z)\in\mathbb Z_+^V\times\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal P_{\mathrm{odd}}(V)}\text{ such that }\{U:z_U>0\}\text{ is laminar}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum-Weight Matching Dual Formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative real edge weights; dual variables correspond to vertices and odd vertex subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a graph and \(w\in\mathbb R_+^E\). Then
\[
\max_{M\text{ matching}}w(M)=
\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V}y_v+\sum_{U\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{odd}}(V)}z_U\left\lfloor\frac{|U|}{2}\right\rfloor:
\begin{array}{l}
y\in\mathbb R_+^V,\ z\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal P_{\mathrm{odd}}(V)},\\
\sum_{v\in V}y_v\chi^{\delta(v)}+\sum_{U\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{odd}}(V)}z_U\chi^{E[U]}\ge w
\end{array}\right\},
\]
where the vector inequality is componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative edge weights, the maximum weight of a matching equals the minimum cost of nonnegative vertex and odd-set multipliers whose combined incidence vector dominates the weight vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{M\text{ matching}}w(M)=\min_{\substack{y,z\ge0\\\sum_v y_v\chi^{\delta(v)}+\sum_U z_U\chi^{E[U]}\ge w}}\left(\sum_v y_v+\sum_U z_U\lfloor|U|/2\rfloor\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Antiblocker Representation Associated with the Matching Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the matching-inequality antiblocker and gives its convex-hull representation by substars and normalized nonempty edge sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\), and let
\[
Q:=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^E:x(M)\leq 1\text{ for every matching }M\}.
\]
Then \(Q\) is the antiblocking polyhedron of the matching polytope, and
\[
Q=\operatorname{conv}\left(\{\chi^S:S\subseteq\delta(v)\text{ for some }v\in V\}\cup\left\{\frac{\chi^F}{\left\lfloor |\bigcup F|/2\right\rfloor}:\varnothing\neq F\subseteq E\right\}\right),
\]
where \(\bigcup F\) is the set of vertices covered by \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative vectors having total value at most one on every matching form the antiblocker of the matching polytope. This polyhedron is the convex hull of incidence vectors of substars and incidence vectors of nonempty edge sets normalized by the floor of half the number of vertices they cover.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q=\operatorname{conv}\left(\{\chi^S:S\text{ is a substar}\}\cup\left\{\frac{\chi^F}{\lfloor|\bigcup F|/2\rfloor}:\varnothing\neq F\subseteq E\right\}\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Majorization Characterization of Tight Odd Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of tightness using equal-sized families of odd and trivial cuts with multiplicities counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a graph with a perfect matching, and let \(C\) be an odd cut of \(G\). Then \(C\) is tight if and only if there exist a family \(\mathcal F\) of odd cuts containing \(C\) and a family \(\mathcal F'\) of trivial cuts such that \[|\mathcal F|=|\mathcal F'|\quad\text{and}\quad \mathcal F'\text{ majorizes }\mathcal F.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a graph with a perfect matching, an odd cut C is tight exactly when C belongs to a family of odd cuts that is majorized by an equally large family of trivial cuts, with multiplicities counted.
assumptions_latex: C\text{ is an odd cut of }G
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C\text{ is tight}\iff \exists\mathcal F,\mathcal F'\;[C\in\mathcal F,\;\mathcal F'\text{ consists of trivial cuts},\;|\mathcal F|=|\mathcal F'|,\;\mathcal F'\text{ majorizes }\mathcal F]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perfect-Matching Polytope and Odd Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the perfect-matching polytope, identifies its face relation to the matching polytope, and records the odd-cut terminology used in its inequality description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G\), \[PM(G):=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^M:M\text{ is a perfect matching of }G\}.\] If \(p=|V(G)|\), then \[PM(G)=M(G)\cap\{x:\mathbf1^Tx=p/2\},\] so \(PM(G)\) is a face of \(M(G)\); if \(p\) is odd, then \(PM(G)=\varnothing\). When \(p\) is even, an odd cut is \(\delta(S)\) for which both \(S\) and \(V(G)\setminus S\) have odd cardinality. These sets are its shores, and the odd cut is trivial when one shore is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perfect-matching polytope is the convex hull of perfect-matching incidence vectors and is obtained as the maximum-cardinality face of the matching polytope. It is empty for odd-order graphs. In an even-order graph, an odd cut has two odd shores and is trivial when one shore is a single vertex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: PM(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^M:M\text{ is perfect}\}=M(G)\cap\{x:\mathbf1^Tx=p/2\},\qquad p\text{ odd}\Rightarrow PM(G)=\varnothing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edmonds' Perfect-Matching Polytope Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear description by degree equations, odd-cut inequalities, and nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\). For \(F\subseteq E\), write \(x(F)=\sum_{e\in F}x_e\), and for \(W\subseteq V\), let \(\delta(W)=\{ij\in E:i\in W,\ j\in V\setminus W\}\). Then \[\operatorname{PM}(G)=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^E:\ x(\delta(\{v\}))=1\ \forall v\in V,\ x(\delta(W))\ge1\ \forall W\subseteq V\text{ with }|W|\text{ odd},\ x_e\ge0\ \forall e\in E\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perfect-matching polytope consists exactly of the nonnegative edge vectors whose incident-edge sum is one at every vertex and whose value across every odd cut is at least one.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edmonds's Perfect-Matching Polytope Description
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete linear description of the convex hull of perfect-matching incidence vectors in an undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph, and let \(\mathcal A\) denote the odd-cardinality subsets of \(V\). Then
\[
\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^M:M\text{ is a perfect matching of }G\}
=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^E:\begin{array}{ll}x_e\ge 0&(e\in E),\\ x(\delta(v))=1&(v\in V),\\ x(\delta(A))\ge 1&(A\in\mathcal A)\end{array}\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an undirected graph, the convex hull of its perfect-matching incidence vectors is exactly the set of nonnegative edge vectors having degree one at every vertex and value at least one on every odd vertex cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{\mathrm{PM}}(G)=\{x\in\mathbb R^E:x_e\ge0\ (e\in E),\ x(\delta(v))=1\ (v\in V),\ x(\delta(A))\ge1\ (A\in\mathcal A)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perfect-matching polytope and its basic relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the perfect-matching polytope of an arbitrary graph and records the validity and general insufficiency of the nonnegativity and degree equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph \(G=(V,E)\), the perfect-matching polytope is \(P_{\mathrm{pm}}(G)=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^M:M\text{ is a perfect matching of }G\}\subseteq\mathbb R^E\). Every \(x\in P_{\mathrm{pm}}(G)\) satisfies \(x_e\ge 0\) for all \(e\in E\) and \(x(\delta(v))=1\) for all \(v\in V\). These constraints are not sufficient for general graphs; in particular, they do not describe the perfect-matching polytope of \(K_3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perfect-matching polytope is the convex hull of the incidence vectors of perfect matchings. Its points satisfy edge nonnegativity and unit incident-edge weight at every vertex, but those constraints are insufficient for general graphs, including the triangle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{\mathrm{pm}}(G):=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^M:M\text{ is a perfect matching of }G\}\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^E:x_e\ge0\ \forall e\in E,\ x(\delta(v))=1\ \forall v\in V\},\quad P_{\mathrm{pm}}(K_3)\ne\{x\in\mathbb R^{E(K_3)}:x_e\ge0\ \forall e,\ x(\delta(v))=1\ \forall v\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(P_{PM}(G)\) is a polytope, every nonempty face is exposed: there exist \(c\in\mathbb R^E\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\) such that \[F=\{x\in P_{PM}(G):\langle c,x\rangle=\alpha\},\qquad \alpha=\max_{x\in P_{PM}(G)}\langle c,x\rangle.\] Since the vertices of \(P_{PM}(G)\) are perfect-matching incidence vectors, \(F\) equals the convex hull of those \(\chi^M\) whose perfect matchings maximize \(c(M)\). Equivalently, a face can be obtained by imposing equality on a collection of valid nonnegativity and odd-cut inequalities, together with the degree equations already satisfied throughout the polytope; redundant tight constraints do not change the face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonempty face is the convex hull of perfect matchings optimal for some edge weights and can be specified by constraints that are tight throughout that face.

knowledge_statements.title: Polytope Dimension Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensions of the matching and perfect-matching polytopes in their natural edge-coordinate spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph. The matching polytope \(P_M(G)\subseteq\mathbb R^E\) is full-dimensional and satisfies \(\dim P_M(G)=|E|\). Suppose that \(G\) has a perfect matching, let \(E^*\) be the set of edges occurring in at least one perfect matching, and put \(H=(V,E^*)\). If \(b(H)\) is the number of bipartite connected components of \(H\), then the affine hull of \(P_{PM}(G)\) is defined by \(x_e=0\) for \(e\notin E^*\) and \(x(\delta_H(v))=1\) for \(v\in V\), and \[\dim P_{PM}(G)=|E^*|-|V|+b(H).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The matching polytope has dimension equal to the number of edges. If the graph has a perfect matching, the perfect-matching polytope has dimension equal to the number of allowed edges minus the number of vertices plus the number of bipartite connected components of the allowed-edge graph.
assumptions_latex: For the perfect-matching formula, \(G\) has at least one perfect matching.

notation.meaning: Edges contained in at least one perfect matching of G.

children.title: Odd-Set Inequality Family
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral restrictions indexed by odd vertex subsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Set Inequality Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Odd-cardinality constraints in Edmonds' description of the general matching polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), every matching-incidence vector satisfies, for each odd set \(S\subseteq V\), \[x(E(S))\leq \left\lfloor\frac{|S|}{2}\right\rfloor=\frac{|S|-1}{2}.\] Together with \(x_e\geq0\) for \(e\in E\) and \(x(\delta(v))\leq1\) for \(v\in V\), all these odd-set inequalities describe the matching polytope: \[P_M(G)=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^E: x\geq0,\ x(\delta(v))\leq1\ \text{for all }v,\ x(E(S))\leq\frac{|S|-1}{2}\ \text{for all odd }S\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An odd vertex set contains at most half its vertices, rounded down, as matching edges; these inequalities complete the matching-polytope description.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(E(S))\leq (|S|-1)/2\), and the displayed system defines \(P_M(G)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Blossom Facet Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facet status of odd-set inequalities for complete-graph matching polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\geq3\) and let \(P_M(K_n)\subseteq\mathbb R^{E(K_n)}\) be the matching polytope of the complete graph. For every odd set \(S\subseteq V(K_n)\) with \(|S|\geq3\), the blossom inequality \[x(E(S))\leq\frac{|S|-1}{2}\] defines a facet of \(P_M(K_n)\). Thus the odd-set family supplies genuine non-degree facets even though every integral matching automatically satisfies each member.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a complete graph, every odd-set inequality on at least three vertices defines a facet of the matching polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(E(S))\leq (|S|-1)/2\) is facet-defining for \(P_M(K_n)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Facet-Defining Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A standard graph-theoretic regime for an odd-set inequality to define a matching-polytope facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) and let \(S\subseteq V\) be odd with \(|S|\geq3\). If the induced graph \(G[S]\) is factor-critical and 2-vertex-connected, then the valid inequality \[x(E(S))\leq\frac{|S|-1}{2}\] defines a facet of the matching polytope \(P_M(G)\). Here factor-critical means that \(G[S]-s\) has a perfect matching for every \(s\in S\). In particular, complete induced subgraphs of odd order at least three satisfy this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An odd-set inequality is facet-defining when its induced subgraph is factor-critical and 2-vertex-connected; odd complete subgraphs are standard examples.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq V\) is odd, \(|S|\geq3\), and \(G[S]\) is factor-critical and 2-vertex-connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(E(S))\leq (|S|-1)/2\) defines a facet of \(P_M(G)\).

notation.meaning: Subgraph of G induced by S.

children.title: Redundant Odd-Set Constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Odd-Set Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A structural class of odd-set inequalities implied by vertex-degree constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\), and let \(S\subseteq V\) be an odd set such that \(G[S]\) is bipartite with bipartition \((A,B)\), where \(|A|\leq|B|\). Every \(x\in\mathbb R^E\) satisfying \(x\geq0\) and \(x(\delta(v))\leq1\) for all \(v\in V\) also satisfies \[x(E(S))\leq\frac{|S|-1}{2}.\] Thus the odd-set inequality indexed by \(S\) is redundant in the matching-polytope system. For a singleton odd set, it reduces to \(0\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an odd set induces a bipartite graph, its odd-set inequality follows from nonnegativity and the vertex-degree inequalities and is therefore redundant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x(E(S))\leq(|S|-1)/2\) is implied by nonnegativity and the vertex-degree constraints.

notation.meaning: A bipartition of the induced graph on S.
Edges of G with both endpoints in S.

knowledge_statements.title: Cunningham–Marsh Total-Dual-Integrality Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total dual integrality of Edmonds' general matching-polytope system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), the system \(x_e\geq0\), \(x(\delta(v))\leq1\), and \(x(E(S))\leq(|S|-1)/2\) for all odd \(S\subseteq V\) is totally dual integral. Equivalently, for every integral weight vector \(w\in\mathbb Z^E\) for which the primal maximum is finite, the dual \[\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V}y_v+\sum_{S\text{ odd}}\frac{|S|-1}{2}z_S:\ y_u+y_v+\sum_{S\text{ odd}:\,u,v\in S}z_S\geq w_{uv},\ y,z\geq0\right\}\] has an integral optimum \((y,z)\). Consequently the system defines an integral polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The degree, nonnegativity, and odd-set system for general matchings is TDI, so every integral edge-weight objective admits an integral optimal dual solution.
assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb Z^E\) and the primal optimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matching-polytope system is totally dual integral and its dual has an integral optimum for integral \(w\).

notation.meaning: Dual variable for the degree inequality at v.
Dual variable for the odd-set inequality indexed by S.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Total Dual Integrality of the Matching-Polytope System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: TDI property of the nonnegativity, vertex-degree, and nontrivial odd-set inequality system for the general matching polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph, and let \(\mathcal A\) denote the odd-cardinality subsets of \(V\). The system
\[
x_e\ge0\quad(e\in E),\qquad
x(\delta(v))\le1\quad(v\in V),\qquad
x(E(G[A]))\le\frac{|A|-1}{2}\quad(A\in\mathcal A,\ |A|>1)
\]
is totally dual integral.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left\{x_e\ge0\ (e\in E),\ x(\delta(v))\le1\ (v\in V),\ x(E(G[A]))\le\frac{|A|-1}{2}\ (A\in\mathcal A,\ |A|>1)\right\}\text{ is TDI}.

children.title: Odd-Set Separation
children.top_down_role: Detection of violated odd-set constraints for candidate fractional points.

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Set Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong separation of odd-set inequalities through a minimum odd-cut computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rational vector \(x\in\mathbb Q^E\) satisfying \(x\geq0\) and \(x(\delta(v))\leq1\). Form an auxiliary graph \(H\) by adjoining a root \(r\), assigning capacity \(x_e\) to every original edge, and capacity \(1-x(\delta(v))\) to \(rv\). Find an odd-cardinality set \(S\subseteq V\) minimizing the cut capacity \(c_H(\delta_H(S))\). If its value is below \(1\), output \(x(E(S))\leq(|S|-1)/2\) as violated; otherwise certify that no odd-set inequality is violated. Indeed, \(c_H(\delta_H(S))=|S|-2x(E(S))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a rooted capacitated graph and find a minimum odd cut; value below one identifies a violated odd-set inequality, otherwise none exists.
assumptions_latex: A polynomial-time minimum odd-cut routine is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a violated odd-set inequality or certifies that all such inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: Capacity of the auxiliary cut determined by S.

children.title: Matching-Polytope Optimization
children.top_down_role: Linear optimization over general matching polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.title: Matching-Polytope Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear optimization over the general matching polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) and rational weights \(w\in\mathbb Q^E\), solve \[\max\{w^Tx:x\in P_M(G)\}.\] Apply a polynomial-time strong separation oracle to the nonnegativity, degree, and odd-set inequalities and use the optimization-from-separation method. The returned optimum may be chosen as an extreme point; because \(P_M(G)\) is integral, it equals \(\chi^M\) for a matching \(M\). Thus the output matching satisfies \(w(M)=\max\{w(N):N\text{ is a matching of }G\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize any rational linear objective over the matching polytope by separation; integrality ensures that an optimal extreme point is an actual matching.
assumptions_latex: A polynomial-time strong separation oracle for \(P_M(G)\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal matching \(M\) maximizing \(w(M)\) is obtained in polynomial time.

children.title: Separation–Optimization Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Oracle-level relationship between polyhedral separation plus optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation–Optimization Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle equivalence for rational, well-described polyhedra, specialized to matching polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a nonempty rational polytope with a known polynomial bound on facet encoding lengths. Strong separation over \(P\) and strong linear optimization over \(P\) are polynomial-time oracle equivalent: either oracle, together with the encoding bound, implements the other in time polynomial in \(d\), the input encoding length, and the oracle running time. Consequently, polynomial-time separation of the odd-set system yields polynomial-time weighted matching-polytope optimization, while a strong optimization oracle yields a strong separator for the same polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a well-described rational polytope, strong separation and strong linear optimization reduce to one another in polynomial time; this applies to matching polytopes.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a nonempty rational polytope.
A polynomial facet-complexity bound for \(P\) is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong separation over \(P\) is polynomial-time equivalent to strong linear optimization over \(P\).

notation.meaning: A rational polytope supplied through an oracle and encoding bound.

children.title: Minimum Odd-Cut Connection
children.top_down_role: Connection between odd-set separation plus minimum odd-cut structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum Odd-Cut Connection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact representation of odd-set slack as a rooted auxiliary cut capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\), and let \(x\in\mathbb R^E\) satisfy \(x\geq0\) and \(x(\delta_G(v))\leq1\) for every \(v\in V\). Form a graph \(H\) by adjoining a root \(r\) to \(G\). Assign capacity \(c_e=x_e\) to each \(e\in E\) and capacity \(c_{rv}=1-x(\delta_G(v))\) to each root edge \(rv\). For every \(S\subseteq V\), \[c(\delta_H(S))=x(\delta_G(S))+\sum_{v\in S}\bigl(1-x(\delta_G(v))\bigr)=|S|-2x(E(S)).\] Therefore, when \(|S|\) is odd, the odd-set inequality indexed by \(S\) is violated exactly when the corresponding auxiliary cut has capacity less than \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The slack of an odd-set inequality is represented by an auxiliary rooted-cut capacity; a violation is exactly an odd-cardinality cut of capacity below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For odd \(S\subseteq V\), \(x(E(S))>(|S|-1)/2\) if and only if \(c(\delta_H(S))<1\).

notation.meaning: Graph obtained from G by adjoining root r and all root edges.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Matchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-relaxation definition of a fractional matching in a general graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), a fractional matching is a vector \(x\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^E\) satisfying \[\sum_{e\in\delta(v)}x_e\leq1\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.\] Its cardinality is \(x(E)=\sum_{e\in E}x_e\), and its weight under \(w\in\mathbb R^E\) is \(w^Tx\). The fractional matching polytope is \[P_{FM}(G)=\{x\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^E:x(\delta(v))\leq1\text{ for every }v\in V\}.\] It is the degree relaxation obtained by omitting the odd-set inequalities from the matching-polytope description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional matching assigns nonnegative edge values so that the total value incident to every vertex is at most one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{FM}(G)=\{x\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^E:x(\delta(v))\leq1\text{ for every }v\in V\}\).

children.title: Fractional Covers
children.top_down_role: Cover-side fractional structures associated with matching relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Covers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-cover LP dual to the maximum-cardinality fractional matching relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), a fractional vertex cover is a vector \(y\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^V\) such that \[y_u+y_v\geq1\qquad\text{for every }uv\in E.\] Its value is \(y(V)=\sum_{v\in V}y_v\). More generally, for \(w\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^E\), a fractional cover of the edge requirements \(w\) is a vector \(y\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^V\) satisfying \(y_u+y_v\geq w_{uv}\) for every \(uv\in E\). The program \[\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V}y_v:y\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^V,\ y_u+y_v\geq w_{uv}\text{ for every }uv\in E\right\}\] is the linear-programming dual of maximizing \(w^Tx\) over the fractional matching polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional cover gives nonnegative vertex weights whose endpoint sum covers every edge requirement; its minimum-value program is dual to weighted fractional matching.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^V\) is a fractional vertex cover exactly when \(y_u+y_v\geq1\) for every \(uv\in E\).

children.title: Matching–Cover Duality
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between the fractional matching side and the fractional cover side.

knowledge_statements.title: Matching–Cover Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted LP duality between fractional matchings and fractional vertex covers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph and let \(c\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{E}\). Then
\[
\max\left\{\sum_{e\in E}c_e x_e:x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{E},\ \sum_{e\in\delta(v)}x_e\le1\ \text{for every }v\in V\right\}
=
\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V}y_v:y\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{V},\ y_u+y_v\ge c_{uv}\ \text{for every }uv\in E\right\}.
\]
Both optima are attained. Thus the maximum weight of a fractional matching equals the minimum weight of a fractional vertex cover for edge demands \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum weight fractional matching equals the minimum fractional vertex-cover cost for the corresponding edge demands.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nu_f(G,c)=\tau_f(G,c)\), with both linear-programming optima attained.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Integrality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact integrality boundary for the degree-constrained fractional matching polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), define
\[
P_f(G)=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{E}:\sum_{e\in\delta(v)}x_e\le1\ \text{for every }v\in V\right\}.
\]
Every extreme point of \(P_f(G)\) is integral if and only if \(G\) is bipartite. Consequently, degree and nonnegativity constraints describe the matching polytope precisely for bipartite graphs. If \(G\) is nonbipartite, a shortest odd cycle is chordless, and assigning \(1/2\) to its edges and \(0\) elsewhere yields a nonintegral extreme point of \(P_f(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The degree relaxation is integral exactly for bipartite graphs; an odd cycle produces a half-integral extreme point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_f(G)\) is integral if and only if \(G\) is bipartite.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Half-integral extreme-point structure of the fractional matching polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a graph and \(x\in\operatorname{FPM}(G)\). knowledge_statements.title: Half-Integral Extreme-Point Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point classification for the fractional matching polytope with only degree constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph, and let \(x\) be an extreme point of
\[
P_f(G)=\left\{z\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{E}:\sum_{e\in\delta(v)}z_e\le1\ \text{for every }v\in V\right\}.
\]
Then \(x_e\in\{0,1/2,1\}\) for every \(e\in E\). The edges with value \(1\) form a matching, while the edges with value \(1/2\) form a vertex-disjoint union of odd cycles disjoint from those value-one edges. Conversely, every vector having this structure is an extreme point of \(P_f(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every extreme fractional matching consists of disjoint unit edges and vertex-disjoint odd cycles whose edges have value one-half.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is half-integral, and its fractional support is a vertex-disjoint union of odd cycles.

knowledge_statements.title: Odd-Cycle Relaxation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp cardinality gap caused by omitting odd-set inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the odd cycle \(C_{2k+1}\), where \(k\ge1\), the vector assigning \(x_e=1/2\) to every edge satisfies all fractional matching degree constraints and has value \((2k+1)/2\). Every integral matching has at most \(k\) edges, and a matching of size \(k\) exists. Hence
\[
\frac{\nu_f(C_{2k+1})}{\nu(C_{2k+1})}=\frac{2k+1}{2k}=1+\frac{1}{2k}.
\]
The ratio is maximized by the triangle, where it equals \(3/2\). The missing odd-set inequality is \(x(E(C_{2k+1}))\le k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An odd cycle has fractional value one-half above its matching number; the triangle gives the largest cycle ratio, three-halves.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tutte-matrix rank characterization of matching number
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic algebraic representation of maximum matching cardinality in an arbitrary graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\). Assign an indeterminate \(x_e\) to every \(e\in E\), and form the symbolic skew-symmetric Tutte matrix \(M\), indexed by \(V\), with opposite entries \(M_{uv}=\pm x_e\) when \(e=\{u,v\}\in E\) and \(M_{uv}=0\) otherwise. Then \(\operatorname{rank}M=2\nu(G)\), where \(\nu(G)\) is the matching number of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank of a graph's symbolic skew-symmetric Tutte matrix equals twice its maximum matching size.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is the associated symbolic skew-symmetric Tutte matrix}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}M=2\nu(G)

knowledge_statements.title: Algebraic Perfect-Matching Existence Testing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Tutte-matrix identity test for perfect-matching existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a graph \(G\) on vertices \(1,\ldots,n\). Introduce commuting indeterminates \(z_{ij}\) for edges with \(i<j\), and initialize the skew-symmetric Tutte matrix \(T(G)\) by \(T_{ij}=z_{ij}\), \(T_{ji}=-z_{ij}\) when \(ij\in E(G)\), and \(T_{ij}=0\) otherwise. Compute whether \(\det T(G)\) is the zero polynomial. Output “perfect matching exists” exactly when it is nonzero. This is correct because
\[
G\text{ has a perfect matching}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \det T(G)\not\equiv0.
\]
For odd \(n\), the determinant vanishes and the output is negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct the symbolic Tutte matrix and test whether its determinant is identically zero; nonvanishing is equivalent to a perfect matching.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite loopless undirected graph.
Polynomial arithmetic is over a field of characteristic different from \(2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns yes if and only if \(G\) has a perfect matching.

notation.meaning: symbolic skew-symmetric Tutte matrix of G

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symbolic Tutte-matrix criterion is standard and the algorithm kind fits the existence-testing leaf, but the record has no citation. An authoritative source with a theorem or section/page locator is required before the determinant criterion can be accepted.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Algebraic Matching Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided-error construction by random Tutte evaluation and algebraic self-reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input an even-order graph \(G
e\varnothing\) and a finite field \(\mathbb F_q\) of odd characteristic. Independently substitute uniform elements of \(\mathbb F_q\) for the Tutte variables, obtaining \(A
\). If \(\det A=0\), report failure and resample. Otherwise choose an edge \(uv\) with \(A_{uv}\ne0\) and \(\det A[V\setminus\{u,v\}]\ne0\), output \(uv\), delete \(u,v\), and repeat on the indicated principal submatrix until no vertices remain. The output edges form a perfect matching. If one initial evaluation is used, a graph having a perfect matching is rejected with probability at most \(n/q\); resampling gives a Las Vegas construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly evaluate the Tutte matrix, then repeatedly select an edge whose complementary principal minor stays nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: Random field substitutions are independent and uniform.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful run outputs a perfect matching; when one evaluation is attempted, false failure has probability at most \(n/q\).

notation.meaning: random numerical evaluation of the Tutte matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction requires an authoritative algorithm locator to verify the complementary-minor selection rule, reuse of one random evaluation, and the stated n/q bound. The Las Vegas claim must also be scoped to graphs promised to have a perfect matching, since perpetual resampling does not terminate on a graph without one.

knowledge_statements.title: Pfaffian Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pfaffian expansion of a skew-oriented weighted adjacency matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) have \(V=\{1,\ldots,2m\}\), fix an orientation, and assign commuting weights \(w_e\). Define the skew-symmetric matrix \(K\) by \(K_{ij}=w_{ij}\) if \(i\to j\), \(K_{ij}=-w_{ij}\) if \(j\to i\), and \(K_{ij}=0\) if \(ij\notin E\). Then
\[
\operatorname{Pf}(K)=\sum_{M\in\mathcal M_{m perf}(G)}s_K(M)\prod_{e\in M}w_e,
\qquad
\det K=\operatorname{Pf}(K)^2,
\]
where \(s_K(M)\in\{-1,1\}\) is determined by the vertex order and orientation. Under a Pfaffian orientation, all nonzero matching terms have one common sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Pfaffian of an oriented skew adjacency matrix is a signed generating function for perfect matchings, and its square is the determinant.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite graph on an even, linearly ordered vertex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Pf}(K)\) is the signed perfect-matching polynomial and \(\det K=\operatorname{Pf}(K)^2\).

notation.meaning: set of perfect matchings of G

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The signed perfect-matching expansion and determinant-square identity fit the representation leaf, but no source is cited. A specific authoritative Pfaffian definition, proposition, or page locator is required, including support for the common-sign assertion.

children.title: Pfaffian Orientations

knowledge_statements.title: Pfaffian Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Odd-orientation criterion using conformal even cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G
\) be a graph having a perfect matching. An even cycle \(C\) is conformal, or nice, when \(G-V(C)\) has a perfect matching. An orientation of \(G\) is Pfaffian if every conformal even cycle \(C\) is oddly oriented: when either direction is chosen for traversing \(C\), an odd number of its edges point in that traversal direction. Equivalently, in the Pfaffian expansion of the associated skew adjacency matrix, all perfect matchings have the same sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Pfaffian orientation directs every conformal even cycle oddly, making all perfect-matching terms in the Pfaffian share one sign.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and has at least one perfect matching.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The orientation is Pfaffian exactly when every conformal even cycle is oddly oriented.

notation.meaning: graph obtained by deleting all vertices of C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conformal-cycle definition and common-sign equivalence are standard and definition is the correct content kind, but the record supplies no inspectable citation. An authoritative definition or theorem locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Characterizations of Pfaffian Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes Pfaffian orientations through matching-sign agreement and odd orientation of nice or alternating cycles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be an even graph and let \(\overrightarrow G\) be an orientation of \(G\). The following are equivalent: (1) \(\overrightarrow G\) is a Pfaffian orientation of \(G\); (2) every perfect matching of \(G\) has the same sign relative to \(\overrightarrow G\); (3) every nice cycle in \(G\) is oddly oriented relative to \(\overrightarrow G\); (4) if \(G\) has a perfect matching, then there exists a perfect matching \(F\) such that every \(F\)-alternating cycle is oddly oriented relative to \(\overrightarrow G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an orientation of an even graph, being Pfaffian is equivalent to all perfect matchings having the same sign, to every nice cycle being oddly oriented, and to the stated conditional alternating-cycle property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{(1)}\iff\text{(2)}\iff\text{(3)}\iff\text{(4)},\text{ where (4) retains the condition that if }G\text{ has a perfect matching, such an }F\text{ exists.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pfaffian Orientations and Pfaffian Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines matching signs, records the Pfaffian counting bound, and defines Pfaffian orientations and graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) have even order, let \(\overrightarrow G\) be an orientation of \(G\), and let \(\Phi(G)\) be the number of perfect matchings of \(G\). For each perfect matching \(F\), define \(\operatorname{sgn}F\) as the sign of its corresponding term in \(\operatorname{pf}(A_s(\overrightarrow G))\). Then \[\left|\operatorname{pf}(A_s(\overrightarrow G))\right|\leq \Phi(G).\] The orientation \(\overrightarrow G\) is Pfaffian when equality holds, and \(G\) is Pfaffian when it admits a Pfaffian orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perfect matching receives the sign of its Pfaffian term. The absolute Pfaffian is at most the number of perfect matchings. An orientation is Pfaffian when equality holds, and a graph is Pfaffian when it admits such an orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left|\operatorname{pf}(A_s(\overrightarrow G))\right|\leq\Phi(G),\qquad \overrightarrow G\text{ is Pfaffian}\iff\left|\operatorname{pf}(A_s(\overrightarrow G))\right|=\Phi(G).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Odd Clockwise-Face Criterion for a Pfaffian Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient face-parity criterion for a connected plane digraph to have a Pfaffian orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\overrightarrow G\) be a connected plane digraph. If the boundary of every face other than possibly the infinite face contains an odd number of edges oriented clockwise around that face, then, for every cycle \(C\), the number of edges oriented clockwise around \(C\) has parity opposite to the number of vertices strictly inside \(C\). Consequently, \(\overrightarrow G\) is Pfaffian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every finite face of a connected plane digraph has an odd number of boundary edges oriented clockwise, then every cycle has a number of clockwise-oriented edges whose parity is opposite to the number of vertices inside the cycle. Consequently, the orientation is Pfaffian.
assumptions_latex: \(\overrightarrow G\) is a connected plane digraph.
The boundary of every face other than possibly the infinite face has an odd number of edges oriented clockwise around that face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall C,\;\#\{e\in E(C):e\text{ is oriented clockwise around }C\}\not\equiv |V(\overrightarrow G)\cap\operatorname{int}(C)|\pmod 2\), and consequently \(\overrightarrow G\) is Pfaffian.
